question: If a patient who dies during general anaesthesia is found to have pre-existing coronary artery disease at autopsy, this finding automatically excludes anaesthetic negligence as a cause of death.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The presence of pre-existing disease does not automatically exclude negligence. Both factors must be evaluated; the final opinion must address whether negligent anaesthetic management materially contributed to death, even in the presence of natural disease.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is FALSE. Pre-existing disease is a confounding factor, not an exclusion. Anaesthetic negligence and natural disease can co-exist as contributing causes of death. The PM opinion must address both and cannot dismiss negligence on the basis of background pathology alone.
